subject: Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces 3.8 Flash at the same price
preview: Gemini glasses from $395, United shuts out AI booking agents, and OpenAI's $10B quarter.
intro: Google shipped most of the news this stretch. The more interesting friction came from elsewhere: companies deciding how much to let AI agents do on their behalf, and a revenue race that depends on how you count.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, replacing 3.8 Flash across its products
stories.body: Hydrogen is now the default in AI Mode and is available in Search, the Gemini app, AI Studio, the Gemini API and business tiers. Paid Pro and Ultra users get it in Antigravity. API pricing is unchanged from 3.8 Flash: $1.50 per million input tokens, $7.50 per million output, with a 1M-token context. Google claims tasks finish 2.5x faster, Terminal-Bench 4.1 rises from 18.2% to 57%, and fabricated claims fall more than 5x. It scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis index, against 50 for Argon.
stories.why: The cheap tier now scores at or above the larger Argon on one index. Per Ars Technica, free and AI Plus users still get 3.5 Flash-Lite, and Carbon and Argon API prices rise to $4/$20 next month.

stories.headline: Google and Samsung open preorders for Gemini glasses from $395, with privacy limits
stories.body: Warby Parker frames start at $395 in the US only; Gentle Monster's six styles start at $449 in the US and South Korea. The glasses have a 12 MP camera and open-ear speakers but no lens display. Google says they won't use the camera if the recording light is covered, Play Store apps can't live stream from them, real-time facial recognition is off, and faces are redacted before video reaches Google. Data isn't encrypted on Google's servers; Private AI Compute is still being worked on.
stories.why: Google is trying to avoid a repeat of the Glass backlash with firm rules. The missing server-side encryption is the gap critics will go after first.

stories.headline: United bars third-party AI agents from booking flights
stories.body: United is updating its booking, ticketing and distribution policies to block unauthorized personal AI agents, both on its own platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators. It cites exposed credentials, unintended purchases or MileagePlus mile use, and federal rules such as a human attesting at check-in that bags hold no banned substances. Agents can still show United flights but can't complete bookings. Southwest is going the other way, making its inventory viewable to ChatGPT users, per CBS News.
stories.why: Airlines are splitting on agent access, and personal assistants will be only as useful as the sites that let them transact.

stories.headline: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly passes $10 billion for the first time
stories.body: Bloomberg, citing anonymous sources, reports OpenAI's third-quarter revenue topped $10 billion, up almost 50% from a reported $6.7 billion in Q2. Its adjusted operating margin reportedly improved from -150% to -109%, and its annual run rate has reached $50 billion. Anthropic said its run rate rose $10 billion in a month to $81 billion at the end of October, and recently reported Q3 revenue of $17 billion.
stories.why: The run-rate comparison is murky: Anthropic counts cloud partners' sales, while OpenAI reports only its share of some partner sales. Compare quarterly revenue instead.

stories.headline: Nvidia privately said chip tracking is possible, while industry publicly called it 'potentially infeasible'
stories.body: Nvidia privately told Rep. Bill Foster that the anti-smuggling chip tracking required by the Chip Security Act is technically possible. An industry group has publicly described the same requirement as 'potentially infeasible'. MIT Technology Review reports the gap between the two positions.
stories.why: It weakens a main industry argument against location verification, and lawmakers pushing for mandates now have Nvidia's own answer to cite.

quickHits.text: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how DNA variations affect different cell types, aimed at tracing the cellular roots of disease.
Families are demanding AI moratoriums in schools after a teen's lawsuit called Gemini a 'suicide coach', hitting Google's school pilot.
SoftBank lost over $3 billion on preordered natural gas turbines meant for AI data centers, which may cap gas-fueled power plans.
British AI chip startup Fractile raised $720M, making it one of the best-funded makers of purpose-built AI chips.
A Podqi study across 151 brands found ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity sometimes recommend imposter or risky retail sites.
Brave Search API now accepts agentic payments through the x402 protocol, so agents can pay per request.
GDC's annual survey finds 40% of game developers use generative AI at work, up from 36% in 2025.
The FAA is expanding an AI advisory tool for air traffic congestion to all US airspace; airlines like it, but the controllers' union wasn't involved.
OpenAI is committing $2 million to research on AI and children's safety, funding shared tools to measure risks and opportunities.
Santosh Janardhan, who joined Meta in 2009 and led its infrastructure, is stepping down.
